# Heterogeneous Compute Placement\chaptersubtitle{Silicon Interconnects, Memory Bus QoS, and Thermal Envelopes}

![**Systems Organ Focus:** Whole-System Heterogeneous Silicon Placement across Cloud, Host MPU, Neural Accelerator NPU, and Real-Time MCU. Physical AI partitions cognitive stages across silicon fabrics based on execution cadence, memory bandwidth, thermal dissipation, and safety isolation boundaries.](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.svg){#fig-locator-ch10 width=100% fig-pos="H"}

*Why does an autonomous robot that runs flawlessly on the test bench suffer violent latency spikes when deployed inside a sealed chassis?*

In cloud software architecture, computation is treated as an abstract, fungible commodity: microservices are deployed into elastic clusters where physical silicon placement is hidden behind virtualization layers. In Physical AI, silicon topology is a non-negotiable physical boundary. Moving bits across off-chip memory buses consumes orders of magnitude more energy than arithmetic, shared memory crossbars choke when camera DMA bursts contend with neural weight streaming, and unmanaged thermal dissipation triggers hardware downclocking that blows past real-time stopping deadlines. Designing an embodied system requires deliberate workload placement—mapping cognitive stages across cloud servers, Linux host processors, neural accelerators, and real-time microcontrollers based on cadence, memory bandwidth, and physical trust boundaries.

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {.callout-objective}
After studying this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Map Cognitive Organs to Silicon Fabrics:** Partition the five sensory-motor organs across Cloud, Host Processor (MPU), Neural Accelerator (NPU), and Real-Time Microcontroller (MCU) fabrics based on cadence ($0.001\text{ Hz} \to 1000\text{ Hz}$), memory bandwidth, and trust boundaries.
2. **Mitigate Interconnect Contention:** Architect hardware AXI Quality-of-Service (QoS) bus arbitration schemes that guarantee microsecond preemption for real-time safety packets over high-bandwidth video DMA bursts.
3. **Implement Deterministic Shared-Memory IPC:** Construct lock-free, zero-allocation circular ring buffers in tightly coupled SRAM using 64-bit atomic sequence counters and explicit cache maintenance operations.
4. **Quantify the Energy Cost of Data Movement:** Balance arithmetic intensity ($\text{FLOPs/Byte}$) against LPDDR5 DRAM access energy ($150\text{ pJ/access}$) using on-chip SRAM model weight tiling.
5. **Model Dynamic Thermal Dissipation & DVFS:** Derive the junction heating differential equation ($T_j(t)$) and design proactive cadence scaling to prevent thermal downclocking cliffs ($>85^\circ\text{C}$).
6. **Evaluate Re-Placement Ripple Effects:** Quantify how migrating neural models between cloud and edge silicon alters network round-trip jitter, battery endurance, and physical stopping clearance envelopes ($d_{\text{stop}}$).
7. **Dissect Wireless Network Latency Collisions:** Analyze the Insulated Cold-Vault Collision autopsy where a $1,420\text{ ms}$ 5G RF blackout caused a 1.2-ton pallet mover to smash into a structural building pillar at $1.8\text{ m/s}$.
8. **Freeze the Workload Placement Ledger:** Author the formal engineering specification (**PLACE-01**) establishing whole-system hardware allocations, interconnect QoS priorities, and thermal derating regimes.

**Core Chapter Takeaway:** Physical AI computation is fundamentally non-fungible; mapping multi-rate cognitive organs across heterogeneous silicon fabrics requires co-designing arithmetic intensity, memory crossbar QoS arbitration, lock-free SRAM mailboxes, and thermal dissipation envelopes to prevent dynamic throttling from breaching real-time control deadlines.
:::


## The Non-Fungibility of Compute in Physical Systems

In modern enterprise software engineering, computation is abstracted behind virtualized infrastructure. Developers write containerized services, dispatch tasks to elastic serverless runtimes, and interact with cloud APIs under the assumption that processing power is fungible. If a database query encounters transient congestion or a network packet drops, execution threads block, retry logic absorbs delays, and garbage collectors sweep memory without physical consequence.

In Physical AI Systems, compute is fundamentally **non-fungible** (@fig-heterogeneous-placement). The moment software interacts with physical mass, inertia, and electrical current, the physical location of silicon determines whether the machine survives:

1. **The Physicality of Latency:** Running a 70-billion-parameter Vision-Language Model in a remote cloud datacenter provides immense semantic capacity. However, routing sensor video over a cellular 5G network introduces stochastic Round-Trip Time (RTT) variance ($50\text{--}1500\text{ ms}$) and unannounced RF signal dropouts. If a 1.2-ton mobile machine traveling at $v = 2.0\text{ m/s}$ loses wireless connectivity for one second, the vehicle coasts unguided for two meters ($d_{\text{coast}} = v \cdot \Delta t = 2.0\text{ m}$), turning a wireless packet drop into an unavoidable collision.
2. **The Physics of Memory Energy:** Moving bits across printed circuit board traces consumes orders of magnitude more electrical energy than performing arithmetic operations on those bits. In modern $7\text{ nm}$ silicon, executing an 8-bit integer multiply-accumulate (MAC) operation consumes approximately $0.2\text{ pJ}$, whereas fetching the operand bytes from off-chip LPDDR5 DRAM consumes $150\text{ pJ}$—a $750\times$ energy disparity.
3. **The Thermodynamic Real-Time Cliff:** Compute chips generate thermal energy ($P = I^2 R + C V^2 f$). In a sealed robotic chassis lacking heavy active cooling, sustained neural inference drives silicon junction temperatures past critical thresholds ($T_j > 85^\circ\text{C}$). Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) circuits automatically cut clock frequencies by up to $60\%$, doubling inference latency and causing the robot to miss its hard real-time stopping deadlines.

![**The Four-Tier Heterogeneous Compute Topology in Physical AI.** System 2 semantic deliberation maps to Tier 3 Linux MPUs or Tier 4 Cloud clusters; System 1.5 trajectory chunking maps to Tier 2 NPUs; System 1 reflex enforcers map to Tier 1 bare-metal MCUs with direct physical routing to motor inverters.](figures/fig09_heterogeneous_placement.svg){#fig-heterogeneous-placement width=100%}

To satisfy these physical constraints, Physical AI partitions cognitive workloads across a **Four-Tier Heterogeneous Silicon Hierarchy** (@tbl-compute-tiers):

| Compute Fabric Tier | Hardware Substrate | Primary Architectural Role | Typical Execution Cadence | Memory Architecture | Physical Trust Level |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- |
| **Tier 4: Cloud / Fleet** | Multi-GPU Datacenter Cluster | Fleet learning, large foundational pre-training, global route planning | $0.001\text{--}0.1\text{ Hz}$ | Terabytes HBM3 / Non-Volatile Storage | **Untrusted:** Non-deterministic WAN latency |
| **Tier 3: Host Processor (MPU)** | 64-bit Multi-Core ARM Cortex-A | Semantic reasoning (VLMs), dynamic frame trees (`tf2`), Linux daemons | $0.5\text{--}10\text{ Hz}$ | 4–16 GB LPDDR5 Unified Memory (UMA) | **Untrusted:** Non-real-time OS jitter ($P_{99} > 100\text{ ms}$) |
| **Tier 2: Neural Accelerator (NPU)** | Systolic Array / Edge Tensor Cores | Spatial affordance tokens (DINOv2), multi-step Action Chunking (ACT, Diffusion) | $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ | On-Chip SRAM Tiling + DRAM DMA | **Untrusted Proposal Service:** High-throughput tensor compute |

## Silicon Interconnects and Memory Bus Contention: AXI Crossbars and QoS Arbitration

In modern embedded Systems-on-Chip (SoCs)—such as the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, Qualcomm Robotics RB5, or Apple M-series silicon—heterogeneous compute engines (CPU, GPU, NPU, ISP, and DMA engines) share a single pool of physical LPDDR5 DRAM through a **Unified Memory Architecture (UMA)** (@fig-uma-contention).

![**UMA Memory Bus Contention and AXI QoS Priority Arbitration.** High-bandwidth camera sensor DMA writes ($>1.5\text{ GB/s}$) and NPU model weight fetches ($20\text{ GB/s}$) contend for shared memory crossbars. Without hardware AXI QoS arbitration, unthrottled DMA bursts starve real-time microcontroller reads, causing $1000\text{ Hz}$ safety loops to miss timing deadlines.](figures/fig09_uma_bus_contention.svg){#fig-uma-contention width=100%}

While UMA eliminates the physical PCIe copying overhead found in desktop computers, it introduces a severe micro-architectural vulnerability: **Memory Crossbar Contention**. In an unmanaged UMA SoC, multiple bus masters issue memory transactions simultaneously across shared AXI interconnect crossbars:

1. High-resolution multi-camera image sensors write raw uncompressed Bayer frames directly to DRAM via MIPI CSI-2 DMA engines ($1.5\text{--}3.0\text{ GB/s}$ sustained).
2. The Neural Processing Unit streams billions of quantized model weights from DRAM into local tensor registers during forward passes ($15\text{--}30\text{ GB/s}$ burst bandwidth).
3. The Real-Time Microcontroller reads joint encoder buffers and writes candidate trajectory waypoints.

When an unthrottled camera DMA burst saturates the memory crossbar, DRAM access latency for CPU and NPU cores spikes by $300\text{--}800\%$. A deterministic $1000\text{ Hz}$ microcontroller thread attempting to read a trajectory waypoint from shared memory is stalled, causing the real-time loop to miss its $1.0\text{ ms}$ control deadline.

To prevent memory starvation, Physical AI architectures configure hardware **AXI Quality-of-Service (QoS)** arbitration registers (`ARQOS` and `AWQOS` signals) at the silicon interconnect fabric:

$$\text{AXI QoS Priority Invariant:} \quad \text{QoS}(\text{MCU Real-Time Reads}) > \text{QoS}(\text{NPU Weight Fetches}) > \text{QoS}(\text{Camera DMA Writes})$$

1. **Real-Time MCU SRAM Reads (`QoS = 15`):** Absolute highest interconnect priority. AXI crossbar arbiters immediately preempt lower-priority transactions to service MCU memory requests within $<50\text{ ns}$.
2. **NPU Tensor Weight Fetches (`QoS = 10`):** High priority, guaranteeing sustained memory throughput to meet $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ action chunking deadlines.
3. **Camera Sensor DMA Writes (`QoS = 4`):** Background priority. Camera DMA streams are buffered in dedicated on-chip FIFO FIFOs and paced onto the crossbar only during memory bus idle cycles, eliminating latency tail blowouts.


## Deterministic Inter-Processor Communication: Zero-Copy Shared SRAM Mailboxes and Lock-Free Ring Buffers

To pass high-rate trajectory chunks ($50\text{ Hz}$) and low-latency safety telemetry ($1000\text{ Hz}$) between the Linux host MPU and the bare-metal MCU without thread blocking, Physical AI rejects traditional operating system IPC primitives (such as sockets, named pipes, or POSIX mutexes). Under Linux, acquiring a contested mutex involves kernel context switches that introduce up to $50\text{ ms}$ of scheduling jitter.

Instead, inter-processor communication is implemented using **Zero-Copy Lock-Free Single-Producer Single-Consumer (SPSC) Ring Buffers** residing in physical internal static SRAM (Tightly Coupled Memory - TCM):

```c
// LOCK-FREE INTER-PROCESSOR COMMUNICATION BUFFER (Shared Static SRAM)
#define SRAM_BUFFER_SLOTS 3
#define CACHE_LINE_SIZE   64

typedef struct {
    // Producer Cache Line (Written by Linux MPU, Read by MCU)
    alignas(CACHE_LINE_SIZE) volatile uint64_t head_sequence;
    
    // Consumer Cache Line (Written by MCU, Read by Linux MPU)
    alignas(CACHE_LINE_SIZE) volatile uint64_t tail_sequence;
    
    // Static Payload Buffer Arena (Zero Heap Allocation)
    alignas(CACHE_LINE_SIZE) trajectory_chunk_t slots[SRAM_BUFFER_SLOTS];
    
    // Cryptographic Lineage and Integrity Check
    uint32_t magic_header;
    uint32_t payload_crc32;
} lockless_sram_mailbox_t;
```

The lock-free mailbox operates under strict memory ordering rules:

1. **Atomic Monotonic Sequence Counters:** The producer increments `head_sequence` using 64-bit atomic operations with release memory barriers (`__atomic_store_n(&head, seq, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)`). The consumer reads the sequence using acquire memory barriers (`__atomic_load_n(&head, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)`), guaranteeing that payload data writes are fully visible before the sequence number updates.
2. **Cache Coherency Line Invalidation:** When bridging non-coherent hardware domains (e.g., an ARM Cortex-A application processor with L1/L2 caches and an ARM Cortex-M7 with tightly coupled memory), software must explicitly execute cache maintenance operations:

$$\text{Producer Write:} \quad \text{write\_payload}() \implies \text{clean\_dcache\_range}(\text{addr}, \text{size})$$

$$\text{Consumer Read:} \quad \text{invalidate\_dcache\_range}(\text{addr}, \text{size}) \implies \text{read\_payload}()$$

3. **Latest-Frame Sampling Semantics:** If the producer publishes action chunks faster than the consumer consumes them, the consumer drops intermediate frames and immediately samples the freshest available sequence, guaranteeing zero latency accumulation.


## Arithmetic Intensity vs. Memory Bandwidth: The Physics of Data Movement

In physical systems design, the total power budget is constrained by onboard battery capacity and thermal dissipation limits. To maximize operational battery life and prevent thermal runaway, algorithms must be optimized for **Arithmetic Intensity** ($I_{\text{arith}}$), defined as the ratio of computational floating-point operations to memory access traffic [@hennessy2019computer]:

$$I_{\text{arith}} = \frac{\text{Total Operations (FLOPs)}}{\text{Total Memory Traffic (Bytes)}} \quad \left[ \frac{\text{FLOPs}}{\text{Byte}} \right]$$

The hardware roofline model dictates whether a neural policy is bound by computational throughput or memory bandwidth:

$$\text{Attainable Performance (FLOPs/s)} = \min\left( \text{Peak Compute Bandwidth}, \; I_{\text{arith}} \times \text{Peak Memory Bandwidth} \right)$$

In standard autoregressive transformer decoding (such as single-token VLA inference), the network fetches multi-gigabyte weight matrices from DRAM to perform a single vector-matrix multiply per token ($I_{\text{arith}} \approx 1\text{ FLOP/Byte}$). The accelerator's tensor ALUs spend $>90\%$ of their time stalled waiting for DRAM bytes to arrive, burning battery power in memory bus I/O pads.

To achieve maximum computational efficiency, Physical AI systems apply three silicon optimizations:

1. **On-Chip SRAM Weight Tiling:** Small, high-frequency trajectory decoders (such as 1D Temporal U-Nets for Diffusion Policy) are quantized to INT8 or FP8 precision, enabling the entire active model weights ($<8\text{ MB}$) to reside permanently inside the NPU's on-chip static SRAM.
2. **Elimination of Off-Chip DRAM Round-Trips:** By keeping intermediate activations in on-chip SRAM across layers, memory bus traffic is reduced to zero during trajectory generation, increasing arithmetic intensity to $I_{\text{arith}} > 150\text{ FLOPs/Byte}$.
3. **Energy Savings:** Operating out of SRAM cuts data movement energy by $98.5\%$, allowing the neural accelerator to sustain $50\text{ Hz}$ action chunking while drawing under $15\text{ Watts}$ of total power.


## Thermal Design Power (TDP) and Dynamic Throttling (DVFS): The Thermal Envelope

All electrical energy consumed by silicon computing substrates is ultimately converted into thermal heat via Joule heating ($P = I^2 R$). In an embodied robot, compute silicon is frequently housed inside a sealed, IP67-rated water-resistant chassis lacking heavy active cooling fans (@fig-thermal-derating).

![**Thermodynamic Junction Heating and the DVFS Downclocking Cliff.** Sustained high-load neural inference dissipates thermal heat. When junction temperature breaches $T_j > 85^\circ\text{C}$, hardware DVFS circuits downclock the accelerator by up to $60\%$, doubling inference latency and causing the robot to miss its real-time stopping deadlines. Proactive cadence scaling manages thermal equilibrium.](figures/fig09_thermal_derating_ripple.svg){#fig-thermal-derating width=100%}

The thermodynamic heat dissipation of the compute die is modeled by the first-order differential equation:

$$C_{\text{die}} \frac{d T_j(t)}{dt} = P_{\text{dynamic}}(t) + P_{\text{leakage}}(T_j) - \frac{T_j(t) - T_{\text{ambient}}}{R_\theta}$$

where $T_j$ is the silicon junction temperature, $C_{\text{die}}$ is the thermal capacitance of the silicon package, $R_\theta$ is the thermal resistance to ambient air, $P_{\text{dynamic}} = \alpha C V^2 f$ is the active switching power, and $P_{\text{leakage}} \propto T_j^2$ is temperature-dependent leakage current.

When sustained neural inference drives the junction temperature past the silicon safety knee ($T_j > 85^\circ\text{C}$), on-chip thermal supervisory circuits trigger **Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS)**. To prevent silicon destruction, the hardware controller downclocks the accelerator:

$$f_{\text{clock}} \leftarrow 0.40 \times f_{\text{nominal}}$$

This sudden $60\%$ frequency collapse doubles trajectory inference latency ($T_{\text{infer}}: 25\text{ ms} \to 60\text{ ms}$), causing System 1.5 to miss its $50\text{ ms}$ action chunk deadline. Actuators are starved of fresh waypoints, intent leases expire, and the robot trips a hard emergency stop.

To eliminate thermal cliff collapses, Physical AI deploys **Proactive Thermal Cadence Scaling**. The firmware monitors on-die thermal diodes: when temperature reaches the warning knee ($T_j \ge 75^\circ\text{C}$), the system proactively scales the trajectory chunking horizon from $H=16$ to $H=32$ and lowers inference cadence from $50\text{ Hz}$ to $20\text{ Hz}$, stabilizing junction heat below the DVFS downclocking threshold without dropping control deadlines.


## Re-Placement Ripple Effects: Evaluating Latency, Power, and Safety Migration

When designing a Physical AI system, architects frequently consider re-partitioning algorithms across compute fabrics (e.g., migrating a Vision-Language Model from an offboard cloud cluster to an onboard edge NPU, or shifting state estimation from an MCU to a Linux thread). 

Every re-placement decision triggers a multi-dimensional ripple effect across latency, power, thermal headroom, and safety (@tbl-placement-tradeoffs):

| Architectural Re-Placement Choice | Primary Advantage | Silicon Latency Impact | Thermal & Power Impact | Safety & Robustness Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Offload System 2 VLA to Cloud / 5G** | Unlocks massive 70B parameter models; saves onboard battery | Adds $50\text{--}1500\text{ ms}$ WAN jitter; subject to RF drops | Reduces onboard compute power by $\sim 30\text{ W}$ | **Vulnerable:** Must enforce hard local MCU fallback leases |
| **Quantize VLA to 3B on Edge NPU** | Fully autonomous offline operation; zero RF network dependence | Deterministic $350\text{ ms}$ local inference latency | Increases onboard TDP by $25\text{ W}$; raises $T_j$ | **Robust:** Immune to wireless dropouts and jamming |
| **Move State Estimation from MCU to Linux MPU** | Access to rich ROS2 / Python sensor fusion libraries | Injects $5\text{--}50\text{ ms}$ OS scheduling jitter | Negligible power delta ($<1\text{ W}$) | **Dangerous:** OS page faults freeze state belief during motion |
| **Move Reflex CBF-QP from Linux to Bare-Metal MCU** | Deterministic sub-millisecond execution ($\text{WCET} \le 175\,\mu\text{s}$) | Reduces safety response latency from $50\text{ ms} \to 1.0\text{ ms}$ | Negligible power footprint ($<0.5\text{ W}$) | **Provably Safe:** Hardware-isolated from OS stalls and crashes |

: Architectural Re-Placement Ripple Effects. Trade-offs across computational capability, latency determinism, thermal dissipation, and physical safety. {#tbl-placement-tradeoffs}

The cardinal rule of Physical AI placement dictates: **Never migrate time-critical safety authority across an asynchronous or non-deterministic boundary**. Semantic deliberation may be offloaded to cloud servers if protected by local intent leases, but real-time state estimation and reflex barrier enforcement must remain permanently anchored to local, bare-metal silicon.


## Systems Failure Anatomy: The Insulated Cold-Vault Collision & 5G Packet Blackout

The destructive physical reality of offloading time-critical policy execution across a non-deterministic wireless network is documented in the forensic autopsy of an autonomous heavy transport AGV.

::: {.callout-autopsy title="The Insulated Cold-Vault Collision"}
**Platform:** 1.2-ton Autonomous Heavy Pallet Mover ($v = 1.8\text{ m/s}$).  
**Failure Mechanism:** To reduce onboard compute costs and power draw, the high-level VLA policy was offloaded to an edge 5G server; entering a cold-storage vault created an RF multipath blackout of $1,420\text{ ms}$.  
**Root Cause:** Drive torque commands remained latched during the wireless dropout without local fallback trajectory caches or an independent MCU stopping supervisor.  
**Physical Consequence:** The vehicle coasted unguided for $2.56\text{ m}$ ($+1.36\text{ m}$ past obstacle clearance), smashing into a steel building pillar at $1.8\text{ m/s}$ ($42{,}000\text{ USD}$ overhaul).  
:::

![The Autonomous Heavy Pallet Mover Platform. Offloading policy execution to a 5G edge server caused a fatal crash when entering a cold-storage vault that blocked RF signals for $1,420\text{ ms}$.](figures/fig09_agv_mover_cropped.jpg){#fig-agv-mover width=100%}

In this industrial incident, a 1.2-ton automated guided vehicle (AGV) was transporting heavy palletized goods across a distribution warehouse at $v = 1.8\text{ m/s}$ (@fig-agv-mover). To minimize onboard thermal dissipation and battery consumption, systems engineers offloaded the multi-camera vision-language-action policy to an edge computing server over a private 5G Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) network.

At timestamp $T + 84.210\text{ s}$, the AGV crossed the threshold into an industrial cold-storage refrigeration vault. The vault walls were constructed of double-sided steel-clad polyurethane insulation panels, forming a virtual Faraday cage. The RF signal-to-noise ratio collapsed immediately, and the 5G connection entered an unannounced $1,420\text{ ms}$ packet blackout.

Onboard the vehicle, the Linux host processor had no local trajectory cache. The motor inverter controller was programmed to hold the last received velocity setpoint until a new command arrived. Lacking an autonomous bare-metal microcontroller monitoring stopping clearance ($d_{\text{stop}}$), the 1.2-ton machine coasted unguided at full speed:

$$d_{\text{coast}} = v \cdot \Delta t_{\text{blackout}} = 1.8\text{ m/s} \times 1.420\text{ s} = 2.556\text{ m}$$

At the entrance of the vault, a structural steel building column was located at a physical clearance of $d_{\text{clearance}} = 1.20\text{ m}$. Because the vehicle traveled $2.56\text{ m}$ without braking, it exhausted the clearance and smashed into the steel column at full speed ($v = 1.8\text{ m/s}$).

The kinetic energy at impact ($E_k = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 1{,}200 \times 1.8^2 = 1{,}944\text{ Joules}$) sheared the front steering kingpin, ruptured high-pressure hydraulic steering lines, and crushed onboard lithium battery modules ($42{,}000\text{ USD}$ overhaul cost). The flight-recorder telemetry ledger is detailed in @tbl-telemetry-ch10.

| Timestamp | Subsystem & Substrate | Recorded State / Telemetry Event | Physical Implication |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$T + 84.210\text{ s}$** | 5G RF Transceiver (Vehicle) | Vehicle crosses cold-storage vault threshold; steel-clad insulation panel blocks 5G signals. | RF signal-to-noise ratio drops to zero. |
| **$T + 84.250\text{ s}$** | Linux Host MPU (Vehicle) | TCP socket enters retransmit timeout; high-level VLA trajectory stream halts. | $1,420\text{ ms}$ communication blackout begins. |
| **$T + 84.500\text{ s}$** | Inverter PWM Controller | Lacking local trajectory cache or MCU watchdog, inverter latches last forward drive torque ($240\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$). | 1.2-ton machine coasts unguided at $1.8\text{ m/s}$. |
| **$T + 85.000\text{ s}$** | Vehicle Chassis / Front Linkage | Vehicle traverses $1.42\text{ m}$, completely exhausting physical clearance ($d_{\text{clearance}} = 1.20\text{ m}$). | Collision unavoidable; zero braking engaged. |
| **$T + 85.630\text{ s}$** | Chassis / Steel Building Pillar | Vehicle strikes steel pillar at $1.8\text{ m/s}$ ($E_k = 1{,}944\text{ J}$). | Steering linkage shears; hydraulic lines rupture ($42{,}000\text{ USD}$ damage). |
| **Root Cause** | *Systems Bottleneck* | Offloading real-time policy authority across an unbudgeted, stochastic wireless network without local trajectory fail-safes. |
| **Architectural Flaw** | *Privilege & Co-Design* | Lack of local MCU heartbeat watchdog and absence of onboard autonomous stopping distance supervisor ($d_{\text{stop}}$). |

## Engineering Contract & The Placement Ledger: Freezing the Hardware Topology

To establish a formal hardware mapping across compute fabrics, the systems architecture defines the **Workload Placement Specification (PLACE-01)** (@tbl-dossier-place-01).

| Subsystem Domain | Architectural Parameter | Guaranteed Invariant & Verification Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tier 1 (MCU) Execution** | `core_type`<br>`clock_hz`<br>`sram_bytes` | ARM Cortex-M7 / Dual-Core Lockstep RISC-V<br>$480.0\text{ MHz} \pm 10\text{ ppm}$<br>$512\text{ KB}$ (Zero Heap / Static Arrays Only - `malloc=0`) |
| **Tier 2 (NPU) Placement** | `model_type`<br>`target_cadence`<br>`sram_tiling_mb` | Diffusion Policy / ACT ($H=16$)<br>$20.0\text{ Hz}$ ($50\text{ ms}$ execution budget)<br>$\ge 8.0\text{ MB}$ dedicated on-chip weight SRAM |
| **Tier 3 (MPU) Placement** | `os_kernel`<br>`max_p99_latency_ms`<br>`dram_alloc_gb` | Linux 6.6 with `PREEMPT_RT`<br>$\le 35.0\text{ ms}$ nominal ($P_{99}$)<br>$4.0\text{ GB}$ LPDDR5 pinned memory (`mlockall`) |
| **Bus QoS Configuration** | `mcu_read_qos`<br>`npu_fetch_qos`<br>`dma_stream_qos` | `QoS = 15` (Highest priority - preemption enabled)<br>`QoS = 10` (Medium-high priority tensor fetches)<br>`QoS = 4` (Throttled background camera DMA) |
| **Thermal Envelopes** | `t_junction_max`<br>`fan_trip_temp`<br>`dvfs_derate_temp` | $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ maximum junction threshold ($T_j$)<br>$65.0^\circ\text{C}$ active cooling trigger<br>$75.0^\circ\text{C}$ proactive cadence scaling |

: The Workload Placement Specification (**PLACE-01**). Quantitative silicon parameters, bus QoS priorities, and thermal boundaries bridging Architecture to Integration. {#tbl-dossier-place-01}

| **Time & Freshness** | Network and OS latency tails ($>1\text{ s}$) create blind execution. | **Strict Local Placement:** System 1 reflexes reside strictly on onboard MCU. |
| **Inertia & Stopping** | Large kinetic momentum requires guaranteed local stopping autonomy. | **Hardware Watchdog Timers ($15\text{ ms}$)** triggering local Category 1 braking. |
| **Actuation & Jerk** | Discrete IPC messages command jagged motor step changes. | **MCU Quintic Spline Interpolation** executed in zero-wait-state SRAM. |
| **Energy & Thermal** | Excessive DRAM accesses and NPU heating cause thermal throttling. | **On-Chip SRAM Model Tiling** and dynamic thermal derating ledgers. |
| **Silicon Determinism** | Shared UMA memory crossbar contention stalls critical threads. | **Hardware AXI QoS Priority Arbitration** (`ARQOS`/`AWQOS`). |

## Chapter Summary and Forward Handoff

This chapter established how cognitive workloads are deliberately placed across heterogeneous silicon fabrics. Physical AI rejects the cloud illusion of fungible compute, mapping multi-rate cognitive stages across Cloud, Host MPU, Neural Accelerator NPU, and Real-Time MCU based on cadence, memory bandwidth, thermal dissipation, and physical trust boundaries.

By enforcing hardware AXI QoS bus priorities, lock-free shared SRAM ring buffers, and local microcontroller fail-safes, we eliminate memory crossbar contention and guarantee that network dropouts never cause physical collisions.

In the following chapter, **Chapter 11 (Runtime Governance and Safety Systems: Hazard Mitigation, Dual-Heartbeat Watchdogs, and Governed Flywheels)**, we explore how physical agents are governed during continuous operations. We examine human-machine supervisory authority, dynamic hazard escalation, dual-heartbeat hardware watchdogs, and governed data flywheels that guarantee continuous operational safety.
